newsitem.title: USA: Brent climbs in late US trade, WTI/Brent tightens.
newsitem.headline: Brent climbs in late US trade, WTI/Brent tightens.

text.p: North Sea Brent climbed in late U.S. trading Tuesday, with a major Wall Street dealer attributed with all of the buying, traders said.
Two full boats of paper March Brent traded at $22.55 and $22.60 a barrel, compared to the IPE settlement price of $22.45.
Three partials also traded a total of 400 times at $22.50, $22.53 and $22.56 a barrel, traders said.
No intermonth spreads changed hands, traders said.
Meanwhile, the pace of North Sea and West African crudes moving into the U.S. Gulf Coast remains sluggish.
"Refiners are in turnarounds and demand is fairly light," one North Sea seller said.
Further surpressing transatlantic activity is the continued narrowing of the spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent.
The spread stood around $1.50-55 a barrel Tuesday afternoon, extending a downward trend that has diminished the economic incentive for transatlantic trade.

The narrowing spread is reflected in the rising price for Brent cargoes offered into the Gulf Coast. The price for March barrels is now around March WTI minus 10 cents, up from a 30 cent discount last week, traders said.
At the same time, demand in Europe is picking up, with wet Brent trading around March Brent plus 30 cents for mid-February barrels, traders said.
In Latin American activity, Chile's state-owned oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) is seeking to buy 960,000 barrels of crude oil for delivery March 16-20, traders said.
The tender will be awarded tomorrow, traders said.
ENAP purchased one cargo each of Ecuadoran Oriente and Nigerian Forcados in its last purchase tender for delivery March 5-10.
Separately, Uruguay's state-owned oil company ANCAP plans to award a crude tender tomorrow for one million barrels of crude.
